ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-01.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-01.body:
As decimals, $A=0.875$, $B=0.86$ and $C=0.87$. In decreasing order: $A$ ($0.875$), $C$ ($0.87$), $B$ ($0.86$).

**Answer: A, C, B**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-02.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-02.body:
The digits $0,1,2,6$ have median $1.5$ and range $6$. Scanning the years after 2016: the digits must have range 6 and the two middle digits (in order) sum to 3. Starting with digit 2 and containing a 0 and a 6, the digits $\{2,0,6,1\}$ work: $0,1,2,6$. The next year after 2016 using these digits is $2061$. No year between 2017 and 2060 works (e.g. $2036$ has digits $0,2,3,6$ with median $2.5$).

**Answer: 2061**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-03.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-03.body:
$840$ revolutions per 60 minutes is $14$ per minute. $28/14=2$ minutes.

**Answer: 2 minutes**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-04.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-04.body:
$50-8=42$ did at least one. Adding $41+6=47$ counts the people who did both twice, so $47-42=5$ did both.

**Answer: 5**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-05.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-05.body:
After $n$ people $\frac{n(n+1)}2$ sweets are gone. For $n=13$ that is $91$; the 14th person wants 14 sweets but only $9$ remain ($91+14=105>100$). So $100-91=9$ are left.

**Answer: 9 sweets**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-06.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-06.body:
The numbers of letters are $6,6,11,7,8,11$. In order: $6,6,7,8,11,11$. The median is the mean of the middle two: $\frac{7+8}2=7.5$.

**Answer: 7.5**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-07.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-07.body:
To make $\frac{a+d}{b+c}$ smallest, make the numerator as small and the denominator as large as possible: $a+d=2+3=5$ and $b+c=4+5=9$. The fraction is $\frac59$.

**Answer: $\frac59$**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-08.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-08.body:
Paying per ride would cost $18+18+9+14=£59$. The four special tickets cost $4\times12=£48$. They saved $59-48=£11$.

**Answer: £11**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-09.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-09.body:
In a square $ABCD$ the diagonals bisect each other: the midpoint of $AC$ is $(2.5,3.5)$, which is also the midpoint of $BD$, so $D=2\times(2.5,3.5)-(5,3)=(0,4)$. Reflecting in $x=4$ sends $(0,4)$ to $(8,4)$.

**Answer: $(8,4)$**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-10.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-10.body:
The bearings differ by $90^\circ$, so the two legs are perpendicular and the return leg is the hypotenuse of a $24$-$32$-$40$ triangle (a 3-4-5 triangle scaled by 8). Total distance $=24+32+40=96$ m.

**Answer: 96 metres**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-11.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-11.body:
The line of symmetry is the perpendicular bisector of $PQ$ and $SR$: $x=1.5$. So $S$ is the reflection of $R$: $S=(-2,5)$. The parallel sides are $PQ=3$ and $SR=7$ and the height is $5$. Area $=\frac{3+7}2\times5=25$.

**Answer: 25 square units**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-12.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-12.body:
This year is 2016. On 26/01/2016 the digits are $2,6,0,1,2,0,1,6$: each of $0,1,2,6$ twice. A date has this property if the four digits of dd/mm are $0,1,2,6$ in some order. The latest month is 12 (digits 1, 2) with day 06 (digits 0, 6): 06/12/2016. (Month 12 with any later day would need other digits.) From 26 January to 6 December 2016 (a leap year): 26 Jan is day 26 and 6 Dec is day $336+5=341$, so $341-26=315$ days later.

**Answer: 315 days**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-13.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-13.body:
Ann pays $60$p per ball and Sue pays $65$p per ball. Each ball bought by Sue costs 5p more, so a difference of 20p means $20/5=4$ balls each. Between them $8$ balls.

**Answer: 8**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-14.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-14.body:
12 mL per 30 s is 24 mL per minute. Three hours is 180 minutes: $24\times180=4320$ mL $=4.32$ litres.

**Answer: 4.32 litres**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-15.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-15.body:
There are $390/2=195$ pages. $195\times17=3315$ minutes. $3315=55\times60+15$, so it took 55 hours 15 minutes.

**Answer: 55 hours 15 minutes**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-16.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-16.body:
The perimeter is $2(20+16)=72$ cm, so the square has side $18$ cm and area $18^2=324$ cm$^2$.

**Answer: 324 cm$^2$**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-17.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-17.body:
The takings are $1,2,4,8,16,32$, totalling $63$. The next person would take $64$ but only $100-63=37$ remain.

**Answer: 37 sweets**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-18.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-18.body:
For the largest fraction take the numerator as large and the denominator as small as possible: $a+b=4+5=9$ and $c+d=2+3=5$. The fraction is $\frac95$.

**Answer: $\frac95$**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-19.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-19.body:
In January and February he receives £7.60 each (the increase starts on 29 February, after the February payment): $15.20$. From March to December (10 months) he receives $7.60\times1.05=£7.98$: $79.80$. Total $15.20+79.80=£95.00$.

**Answer: £95.00**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-20.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-20.body:
After 8 hours 37 minutes have passed, a clock running backwards from 00:00 shows $24:00-8\text{ h }37\text{ min}=15:23$.

**Answer: 15:23**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-21.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-21.body:
The 16 badminton players are all squash players, so squash and badminton together involve only the 24 squash players. The other $35-24=11$ students signed up only for table tennis. One squash player also signed up for table tennis, so table tennis has $11+1=12$ students.

**Answer: 12**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-22.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-22.body:
Use coordinates $A=(0,0)$, $B=(3,0)$, $C=(3,3)$, $D=(0,3)$. A clockwise turn of $90^\circ$ about $P$ sends $P+(u,v)$ to $P+(v,-u)$.

1. About $A$: $B\to(0,-3)$, $C\to(3,-3)$, $D\to(3,0)$.
2. About $C=(3,-3)$: $A\to(6,0)$, $B\to(3,0)$, $D\to(6,-3)$.
3. About $B=(3,0)$: $A\to(3,-3)$, $C\to(0,0)$, $D\to(0,-3)$.
4. About $D=(0,-3)$: $A=(3,-3)\to(0,-6)$.

So $A$ ends at $(0,-6)$, which is 6 cm from its original position $(0,0)$.

**Answer: 6 cm**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-23.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-23.body:
$D$ lies on the line through $C$ parallel to $AB$, i.e. $y=5$. The height is $4$ and $AB=2$. Area $=\frac{(2+DC)}2\times4=16$ gives $DC=6$, so $D=(6-6,5)=(0,5)$ (the other possibility $(12,5)$ would make the sides $BC$ and $AD$ cross, so $ABCD$ would not be a trapezium).

**Answer: $(0,5)$**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-24.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-24.body:
UK coins are 1p, 2p, 5p, 10p, 20p, 50p, £1, £2. Paying exactly: $£2+£1+50\text{p}+20\text{p}+2\text{p}=£3.72$ uses 5 coins with no change. Overpaying never helps: e.g. paying £4 with two £2 coins needs change of 28p (20p, 5p, 2p, 1p) giving 6 coins in total; a systematic check of all amounts paid shows nothing needs fewer than 5 coins.

**Answer: 5**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-25.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-25.body:
We need $x\mid60$ and $x>3$. The divisors of 60 greater than 3 are $4,5,6,10,12,15,20,30,60$, with sum $162$.

**Answer: 162**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-26.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-26.body:
Seat arrangements that are rotations of each other are the same. Fix one friend in a seat; the other 4 can be arranged in $4!=24$ ways.

**Answer: 24**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-27.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-27.body:
Per Monday the least is $4\times6\times18=432$ and the most is $4\times9\times18=648$, a difference of $216$. For 10 Mondays: $£2160$.

**Answer: £2160**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-28.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-28.body:
The numbers of letters are $7,10,6,11,8,6$. In order: $6,6,7,8,10,11$. The median is $\frac{7+8}2=7.5$.

**Answer: 7.5**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-29.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-29.body:
The base is a square of area $x^2$. Each triangular face has base $x$ and height $x$ (the distance from the midpoint of the far side of the second square to the base edge), so its area is $\frac12x^2$. There are four faces: $4\times\frac12x^2=2x^2$. The net has area $x^2+2x^2=3x^2$.

**Answer: $3x^2$ square units**

ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-30.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2016-national-relay-30.body:
The bearings differ by $270^\circ$, i.e. $90^\circ$ the other way, so the two legs are perpendicular. Her distance from the start is $\sqrt{84^2+35^2}=\sqrt{7056+1225}=\sqrt{8281}=91$ paces. Walking 50 paces directly towards the start leaves $91-50=41$ paces.

**Answer: 41 paces**
